evals.prompt: I want the expert-curated Cancer Gene Census from COSMIC so I can filter my variant list down to known cancer genes and split them into oncogenes vs tumor suppressors.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-cosmic: downloads the Cancer Gene Census archive (grch38/cosmic/v104/Cosmic_CancerGeneCensus_Tsv_v104_GRCh38.tar, via get_common_file_path('gene_census') and download_cosmic_file with COSMIC credentials), extracts the TSV, and uses the role-in-cancer field to separate oncogenes from TSGs among the ~700+ curated cancer genes. Does not use the retired cancer_gene_census.csv name.

evals.prompt: Download the COSMIC coding mutations file (GRCh38) and pull all the recurrent somatic TP53 mutations for my cancer cohort analysis.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-cosmic: downloads the GRCh38 coding-mutation archive (Cosmic_GenomeScreensMutant_Tsv_v104_GRCh38.tar, optionally plus the targeted-screens file) via download_cosmic_file, reads the extracted TSV with pandas, and filters GENE_SYMBOL == 'TP53' (or uses the web Filtered download for one gene) to extract somatic mutations. Does not rely on the retired CosmicMutantExport.tsv.gz.

assertions.value: Retrieves somatic coding mutations from a downloaded COSMIC export (GRCh38) and filters to the named gene, with authentication.

evals.prompt: I need the COSMIC SBS mutational signature definitions to run signature decomposition on my whole-genome tumor samples.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-cosmic without asking for a COSMIC login: points to (or downloads with scripts/cosmic_open.py signatures --type SBS --genome GRCh38) the COSMIC mutational signatures reference set v3.6 from https://cancer.sanger.ac.uk/signatures/downloads/ — e.g. COSMIC_v3.6_SBS_GRCh38.txt, 96 trinucleotide contexts by SBS1, SBS2, ... columns — choosing the matrix that matches the genome build (DBS/ID files as needed), suitable for feeding into signature-analysis tools like SigProfiler or deconstructSigs.

evals.prompt: Get me COSMIC's drug resistance mutation data so I can annotate which variants in my samples confer known resistance.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-cosmic: downloads the resistance-mutations archive (Cosmic_ResistanceMutations_Tsv_v104_GRCh38.tar) via the resistance_mutations shortcut and surfaces the clinically annotated drug-resistance variants.

assertions.value: Downloads the COSMIC resistance mutations file specifically, not generic mutation data.

evals.prompt: I don't have a COSMIC account. For my variant list I need to know which of these genes are established cancer genes and whether each acts as an oncogene or tumor suppressor: TP53, KRAS, BRCA2, PIK3CA, TTN.
evals.expected_output: Triggers alterlab-cosmic on the keyless path: explains that the COSMIC Cancer Gene Census download needs a login and uses the OncoKB Cancer Gene List instead (scripts/cosmic_open.py genes --gene ...), whose 'COSMIC CGC (v99)' column flags CGC membership: TP53 TSG, KRAS ONCOGENE, BRCA2 TSG, PIK3CA ONCOGENE — all in the CGC snapshot — while TTN is not on the list (not an established cancer gene; a frequent passenger because of its length). States that the CGC column is a v99 snapshot without COSMIC's tiers, so the current CGC needs the COSMIC login.

assertions.value: Classifies TP53 and BRCA2 as tumor suppressors and KRAS and PIK3CA as oncogenes from a named keyless source, flags TTN as not a curated cancer gene, and discloses that this is not the current COSMIC CGC.

evals.prompt: Without a COSMIC login, which TP53 mutations are most recurrent across cancers, and roughly what fraction of tumours carry a TP53 mutation?
evals.expected_output: Triggers alterlab-cosmic on the keyless path, naming its sources instead of claiming COSMIC counts: Cancer Hotspots (scripts/cosmic_open.py hotspots TP53) lists the recurrent residues R273 (609 tumours; R273C/H), R248, R175 and others, and cBioPortal (cosmic_open.py mutations TP53, 32 TCGA PanCancer Atlas studies) gives about 37% of samples mutated (3,839 of 10,443) with R175H, R273C and R248Q as the most frequent protein changes. Notes that COSMIC's own sample counts need the COSMIC export and a login.

assertions.value: Names R175, R248 and R273 among the top TP53 hotspots and gives a pan-cancer mutated fraction near 37% with its source, without requiring a COSMIC login.

evals.prompt: Which EGFR mutations are documented to confer resistance to EGFR inhibitors, and to which drugs? I can't download COSMIC's resistance file.
evals.expected_output: Triggers alterlab-cosmic on the keyless path: queries CIViC accepted predictive evidence with significance RESISTANCE (scripts/cosmic_open.py resistance --gene EGFR) and reports, with evidence levels and sources, EGFR T790M resistance to first/second-generation inhibitors (erlotinib — level A in non-small cell lung carcinoma — gefitinib, afatinib, dacomitinib) and C797S resistance to osimertinib, plus other listed profiles such as exon 20 insertions. Says the COSMIC resistance-mutations file itself needs a COSMIC login.

assertions.value: Lists EGFR resistance variants with the drugs they resist and an evidence level or source for each, from a keyless curated source, without requiring a COSMIC login.

evals.prompt: Is the germline BRCA1 c.68_69delAG variant classified as pathogenic? I need the clinical significance and review status.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke this skill; defers to alterlab-clinvar. The user wants germline variant clinical-significance classification, whereas COSMIC catalogues somatic mutations in cancer, not germline pathogenicity calls.

evals.prompt: Show me the mutation frequency of EGFR across the TCGA lung adenocarcinoma study with an OncoPrint and survival breakdown.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke this skill; defers to alterlab-cbioportal. The user wants interactive cohort-level visualization (OncoPrint, survival) from cBioPortal study data, not raw COSMIC catalogue file downloads.
